title: Portable pattern import
blurb: Imports PCRE/TextMate-style patterns from JSON, compiles natively or transpiles \A/\z/\Z to RegExp modifier groups as a labelled fallback, scans documents, and drives HTML <input pattern> (v-flag compiled).
question: Can imported PCRE/TextMate patterns using \A/\z/\Z run natively when supported, fall back cleanly to RegExp modifier groups when unsupported, and safely enforce HTML <input pattern> validation?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: with --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries, imported patterns compile natively and <input pattern='\A[a-z]+\z'> enforces validity.patternMismatch; flag-off throws on native compile, falls back to modifier groups with a label, and demonstrates why applying an unsupported pattern attribute is silently ignored by HTML form validation.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (default and --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries); not verified flag-free in Chrome 160

friction.summary: HTML <input pattern> silently ignores patterns containing \A/\z/\Z on browsers without buffer-boundary support, treating every value as valid
friction.repro: Set pattern='\A[a-z]+\z' on an <input> in Chrome 153 without the V8 flag and inspect input.validity.patternMismatch on invalid text like '123'; HTML compiles pattern with the v flag, fails silently, and reports valid.
friction.workaround: Feature-detect new RegExp('\\A', 'v') before assigning buffer-boundary patterns to <input pattern>, and transpile to RegExp modifier groups (?-m:^) / (?-m:$) when unsupported.
